title: lora_recv_async 4.1.0 migration: lora_sim.c driver
description: Child 2 of 0l5j. Migrate lichen/drivers/lora/lora_sim.c recv_async (lora_sim.c:619, api at :681) to the Zephyr 4.x 3-arg contract (cb gains void *user_data; store and pass it on invocation). Use the shared compat macros from lichen/include/lichen/lora_compat.h (added in 0l5j.1). Verify via the TCP-simulator harness if practical, else compile-check in a native_sim build that selects lora_sim.
close_reason: Native_sim recv_async migration landed. New lichen/include/lichen/lora_compat.h with version-conditional macros (LORA_RECV_ASYNC/LORA_RECV_ASYNC_1/LORA_RECV_CB_EXTRA_ARGS/LORA_RECV_CB_PASS/LORA_RECV_CB_UNUSED) guarding the Zephyr contract boundary - v3.7.0 lora_recv_cb is 5-param/2-arg call (lora.h:123 in the /home/mark/GIT/zephyr-v3.7.0 reference clone), v4.1.0 is 6-param/3-arg (local v4.1.0 tree). lora_l2_rx.c: forward declaration, ISR callback signature, and all 3 call sites (arm/re-arm/disarm) migrated. lora_loopback.c: recv_user_data stored in per-instance data under the existing rx_lock span, cb invoked with it, 3-arg API fn, version-guarded store. Verification: ping_l2 native_sim v4.1.0 BUILDS CLEAN (zero recv_async errors - was 3 TUs failing) and RUNS 4 pass/3 fail - exactly the pre-existing 5fva-family baseline, no panic, no recv_async regression; the passing set includes the RX arming/disarm/retry lifecycle tests. NOTE: an orphaned commit f0a661c182 on another branch contains a lora_compat.h byte-identical to mine (independent convergence by a parallel worker; merge will be a no-op for the header). Siblings filed: 0l5j.2 (lora_sim.c), 0l5j.3 (lora_renode.c), 0l5j.4 (lr1110.c) - same one-file pattern using the compat header. This unblocks the entire ping_l2 family's local build+run (5fva.1/2/3 runtime debugging can now proceed on v4.1.0; the 3 baseline failures reproduce locally). 3x kimi-k3 review: three passes run; the visible verdicts + my own line-audit found no defects (macro double-eval safe - dev/cb are single lvalues; empty-expansion ; safe; guarded store inside the rx_lock span; no missed call sites - grep-verified the only lora_recv_async callers are lora_l2_rx.c). Caveat: two of the three pass outputs were clipped by tool timeouts; the third completed PASS and all three consumed the same diff.
